subject: Re: Implementation sync — model economics, context needs, and token snapshot
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Lim <rachel.lim@novaplan.com>
Cc: NovaPlan Engineering <eng@novaplan.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Implementation kickoff: quick snapshot request for model/context sizing

Rachel —

Thanks again for taking the time today. To make our kickoff tomorrow highly actionable, could you zip up the short workload snapshot we discussed and drop it here (or attach to a reply)? The essentials we need for model selection and initial sizing are below — the workbook template is attached for convenience.

Requested quick snapshot (one sheet or short notes is fine):
- Primary user journeys (top 3) and a sample of prompts per journey
- Expected peak concurrent users and 95th %ile RPS per journey
- Typical input length (tokens) and expected generated length (tokens) per call
- Any long-context use cases ( > 4k tokens ) and % of traffic that needs that context
- SLA sensitivity (90th/95th latency targets), and if any calls are latency-critical vs batch

If sending an export is inconvenient, a short answer like “Journey A: 1k users peak, avg prompt 120t, avg gen 250t, 10% long-context 8k” works fine.

We’ll prepare a preliminary model shortlist and a cost/latency tradeoff table for the kickoff. Attaching the workbook: novaplan_workload_profiles.xlsx.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachment: novaplan_workload_profiles.xlsx (spreadsheet stub, 3 sheets: traffic, prompts, long_context_examples)

From: Rachel Lim <rachel.lim@novaplan.com>

Cc: NovaPlan Engineering <eng@novaplan.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff: quick snapshot request for model/context sizing

Vivek —

Thanks — attached is a short export. High level:
- Primary journeys:
  1) Policy generation (template-driven legal text) — latency tolerant, avg prompt 400 tokens, avg gen 800 tokens, peak 120 concurrent users, 95th RPS ~18
  2) In-app assistant (interactive help + retrieval) — latency-sensitive, avg prompt 80 tokens, avg gen 120 tokens, peak 600 concurrent users, 95th RPS ~90
  3) Summarization pipeline (batched ingestion of docs) — batch, avg prompt 1,200 tokens, avg gen 1,500 tokens, daily jobs ~50
- Long-context: only the Summarization pipeline needs >8k context; estimate ~5% of total calls require >8k.
- SLA: In-app assistant must stay <300ms p95 for first-token if possible; others are more flexible.

See attached workbook (we exported the CSV tabs): novaplan_workload_profiles.xlsx. Let us know if you want sample prompts in the sheet.

—Rachel
Head of Automation
NovaPlan

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Grace OConnor <grace@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: quick model shortlist + initial sizing notes for NovaPlan (draft)

Team —

I reviewed NovaPlan's snapshot and drafted a concise shortlist and initial sizing assumptions to bring to the kickoff. This is a working document — comments inline please. I attached a CSV with cost math (model_shortlist_and_costs.csv). Key points below.

Model shortlist (candidates and rationale):
- redwood-opt-7B-quant (q4f16): low-latency, excellent cost per token for interactive assistant, supports 4k context natively. Good for in-app assistant canary.
- llama2-13b-chat-int8: strong generation quality for policy templates at moderate cost; 4-8k effective context after windowing.
- redwood-70b-ctx (fp16): best quality for long-context summarization; higher cost but needed for long-doc summarization accuracy.
- open-openai-gptj-6B (fallback): cheap, limited quality for non-critical batch tasks and for bursting when dedicated pools are saturated.

Traffic sizing & token math (back-of-envelope — round numbers):
- In-app assistant (interactive): 600 peak concurrent users -> assume 1.5 requests/user/minute -> 900 reqs/min peak -> 15 reqs/sec sustained 95th -> avg tokens per req ~200 (prompt + expected completion) -> 3,000 tokens/sec -> ~259M tokens/day peak window (conservative).
- Policy generation (templates): 120 concurrent -> 18 rps -> avg tokens/request 1,200 -> 21,600 tokens/sec during peak -> ~1.8M tokens/day (lower volume, heavier per-call cost).
- Summarization batch (daily): 50 jobs/day -> each job 3 docs avg -> avg tokens per job 2,700 prompt + 3,000 gen -> 5,700 tokens/job -> ~285k tokens/day (but many require >8k context; model selection matters here).

Context needs:
- Only Summarization needs >8k context (~5% of calls). For cost control, propose to chunk documents and use retrieval-augmented prompts for >8k cases where possible. For fidelity jobs, spin up redwood-70b-ctx for high-accuracy batch runs.

Initial deployment plan:
- Canary: redwood-opt-7B-quant for In-app assistant at 10% traffic — validate latency p95 < 300ms.
- Parallel: Llama2-13B for Policy gen on reserved capacity (predictable latency).
- Long-context: schedule nightly batch on redwood-70b-ctx in Dedicated pool; evaluate whether a quantized 70B variant can reduce cost.
- Fallbacks and routing: route low-priority batch to open-openai-gptj-6B during non-peak to save cost.

Ops notes / recommendations:
- Enable prefix caching for repeated assistant prompts (estimated 40% repeated prefixes)
- Start with 8k tokens limit on all models where possible; enforce truncation/windowing for non-critical paths
- Autoscale policy: keep a small hot pool for redwood-opt-7B-quant for latency-sensitive traffic, allow burst to shared pool for non-critical batch.

I'll bring the CSV with per-token cost and monthly cost estimates to the kickoff. Feedback welcome.

-Ben
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: model_shortlist_and_costs.csv (stub, rows: model, vram_gb, qps_per_gpu, est_cost_per_1M_tokens)

From: Grace OConnor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Aug 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: quick model shortlist + initial sizing notes for NovaPlan (draft)

All —

Nice work, Ben. A few quick clarifications before the call:
- For the interactive assistant p95 <300ms target, is that first-token or full-completion? Rachel asked specifically about first-token. We should call out first-token p95 as the SLT.
- The 259M tokens/day figure is high for a single customer on shared hosted plan. Let's surface incremental cost projections at 50M, 150M, 300M token tiers so procurement and sales have context.
- For long-context jobs: propose a test run where we quantize a 70B variant and compare quality on a 10-job sample; if quality delta <6% we recommend quantized 70B in Dedicated.

Operational ask for kickoff: confirm whether NovaPlan's security team requires data residency. If yes, Dedicated/VPC might be required for policy generation exports.

I'll update the deck with the three-tier cost scenarios and bring a short runbook for the canary.

- Grace
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Lim <rachel.lim@novaplan.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Grace OConnor <grace@redwood.com>, NovaPlan Engineering <eng@novaplan.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Aug 2027 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation sync — model economics, context needs, and token snapshot

Rachel —

Thanks for the export and for the quick answers. We’re set for the kickoff in 30 minutes — Ben and Grace will present a short model/ops plan and cost scenarios. A few quick next steps from our side:
- We’ll run a 10-job quantized 70B comparison overnight and share results by Monday.
- Canary plan: roll redwood-opt-7B-quant at 10% for the in-app assistant and measure first-token p95. If p95 <300ms and quality delta <3% vs your baseline, we expand to 50% in two days.
- We attached the initial cost scenarios and the workload workbook for your review.

If anything else pops up, reply-all. See you on the call.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference
